I will keep my land in the familiar `winter wheat -> summer maize` rotation. I would not switch away from it this year because Quzhou County is a typical North China Plain wheat-maize area, most farmland there already follows that system, and the weather pattern fits it: annual precipitation is only about 500 to 556 mm, with most rain falling in July and August, so summer maize can lean on rainfall while winter wheat still gives me a full second grain crop if I irrigate carefully. For wheat, I will use improved seed, rotary till the maize straw back in, keep fertilizer at a moderate but solid level, and irrigate twice around the key stages instead of chasing very high water use. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, seed directly with no-tillage after wheat harvest, give one establishment irrigation if needed, and keep fertilizer focused on stable yield rather than excess input. I am choosing the rates below because they sit close to the North China Plain guidance for winter wheat and Huang-Huai-Hai summer maize, while staying practical for water-saving management in Hebei. Sources I’m relying on: Quzhou cropping and rainfall context from Scientific Reports and Journal of Cleaner Production, irrigation timing evidence for the wheat-maize rotation from Agricultural Water Management, and fertilizer guidance from China’s Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs: https://www.nature.com/articles/srep41587, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959652614000304, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0378377424000611, https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/zxfb/202209/t20220922_6411293.htm, https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/ZZYGLS/202303/t20230314_6423039.htm
